solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicatorNotes.bananas: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A recipe step: soften some bananas to make a light snack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit being soaked, but it is slang for mad. A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of scones, jam, clotted cream and a pot of tea.
annotation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a small afternoon meal, lighter than lunch or dinner.

entries.clue: Perfume ingredient found in Gorbals, amazingly (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: the answer is found sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last four letters of Gorbals run on into the first two of amazingly

annotation.surface: Someone is surprised to learn a perfume ingredient comes from a rough part of Glasgow.
annotation.walkthrough: The Gorbals is a Glasgow district once famous for slums, which makes a perfume source there 'amazing'. 'Amazingly' looks like an anagram indicator but here it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resin used in perfumes.

blocks.note: a flat-bodied sea fish related to the plaice
to thrash about clumsily, as a swimmer out of their depth does

annotation.surface: A fish that struggles in water, which is the one place it should be at home.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that a fish floundering in water is a contradiction, and the flounder is also a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a flatfish of the plaice family, and a verb for thrashing about in water or mud, later any clumsy struggle.

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of 'bite' is its first letter

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: An instruction to hold back a dog that has started to bite.
annotation.walkthrough: CUR is a crossword favourite for a dog, usually a snappish mongrel, which suits a dog that has started to bite.
annotation.definitionFit: To curb something is to hold it in check.

indicatorNotes.heartless: without a heart, the middle letters are cut out

blocks.note: the central pair of an eight-letter word, removed

annotation.surface: A cynical remark that callous cheats are being egged on.
annotation.walkthrough: CHEATERS has eight letters, so its heart is the central pair AT.
annotation.definitionFit: To cheer someone on is to encourage them.

indicatorNotes.when climbing: in a down clue, climbing means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: to stew is to fret and be agitated, and those letters are read from the bottom up

annotation.surface: Timid people get flustered when they have to climb.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a wet is a feeble, ineffectual person.
annotation.definitionFit: Wets are weak, spineless people, so wimps.

entries.clue: Killer whale from California on banks of Oder (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B
indicatorNotes.banks of: a river's banks are its edges, so the outer letters of Oder

blocks.note: CA is the abbreviation for California

annotation.surface: A killer whale from California turns up on a European river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Oder is a river between Germany and Poland, so 'banks' fits the surface as well as picking out its edge letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the killer whale's scientific name is Orcinus orca, and orca has become its everyday name too.

annotation.definitionNote: plural noun for a mass noun: 'in convulsions' means helpless with laughter

indicatorNotes.suffering: the letters are in a bad way and come out in a new order

annotation.surface: A genuine hoodlum is having a fit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Convulsions' looks like the thug's medical symptoms, but it is the helpless shaking of someone in fits of laughter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be 'in convulsions' is to be shaking helplessly with mirth, so the plural stands for the fit itself.

indicatorNotes.struggling: the letters are writhing into a different order

annotation.surface: Saunas are doing badly in a hot Caribbean city.
annotation.walkthrough: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas, where a sauna business might well struggle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Bahamas is a Caribbean nation and this is its capital city.

indicatorNotes.nipping: the animal nips the R, holding it in its jaws

annotation.surface: A creature bites someone on the chest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nipping' looks like the animal biting, and it is: the beast grips the R between its first and second letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Breast and bosom both mean the chest.

entries.clue: Small child’s first to finish article (4)

indicatorNotes.first to finish: the first letter moves to the finish

blocks.note: a mite is a tiny child; these are its letters after the first
the first letter of mite, moved to the finish

annotation.surface: A toddler is first to finish writing a piece.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a child winning a race; 'first to finish' is an instruction instead.
annotation.definitionFit: An item is an article, as a single thing on a list or a piece in a paper.

entries.clue: Poorest chewed on last of hard, thick slice of bread (8)

indicatorNotes.chewed: chewed up, the letters are mashed into a new order
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

annotation.surface: The poorest are left gnawing on a hard, thick slab of bread.
annotation.walkthrough: A doorstep is British slang for a very thick slice of bread, as thick as a doorstep.
annotation.definitionFit: A doorstep sandwich is made with bread cut in thick slabs.

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking mad, so the letters go crazy

annotation.surface: Someone dutifully reports a trip to Barking, a district of east London.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Barking look like the London place; it is 'barking' as in barking mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Obedient and dutiful both describe someone who does what they are told.

entries.clue: Regularly sense journalists love strong drink (8)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

blocks.note: sEnSe, the second and fourth letters
love = zero in tennis scores, O

annotation.surface: A claim that reporters habitually have a taste for hard liquor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strong drink' suggests alcohol, but here it is strong coffee.
annotation.definitionFit: Espresso is a small, concentrated shot of coffee.

entries.clue: Celebration of WI speciality endured by European (8)

indicatorNotes.by: by means next to, so BORE is followed by E

blocks.note: the Women's Institute is famous for its jam
bore = endured, past tense of bear

annotation.surface: A party celebrating the Women's Institute's best cooking, put up with by a visitor from Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation famous for home-made jam.
annotation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large, lively celebration or gathering.

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as reported, spoken rather than written

blocks.note: a breach is a break or rupture

annotation.surface: News of a split in someone's trousers, or worse.
annotation.walkthrough: Breech is an old word for the buttocks, still heard in a breech birth, where the baby comes bottom first.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word for the rump, surviving in 'breech birth' and in breeches, the garment that covers it.

indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the Y is placed behind MOP

blocks.note: a shock of hair is a mop

annotation.surface: Someone still feels low years after a traumatic event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as trauma, but it is a thick mass of hair, a mop.
annotation.definitionFit: Mopy means listless and gloomy, feeling sad.

entries.clue: Virile embraces lead to intimacy, for the most part (6)

indicatorNotes.embraces: MANLY holds I in its arms
indicatorNotes.lead to: the lead of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Hugs from a strong man usually end in something closer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Embraces' reads as hugging in the surface; in the wordplay MANLY simply holds the I between its second and third letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adverb phrase: both mean largely, chiefly.

blocks.note: a lame excuse is an unconvincing one

annotation.surface: Someone complains that a passage of scripture is not persuasive.
annotation.walkthrough: The Book of Lamentations is itself part of the Bible, which helps the surface hang together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to express grief or regret over something.

indicatorNotes.Leaving: H leaves the word, so it is removed

blocks.note: H = husband, the letter that leaves

annotation.surface: A scruffy, casual man walks out on his marriage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a man walking out on his wife; in the wordplay only the letter H walks out.
annotation.definitionFit: An airy manner is casual and dismissive, offhand.

entries.clue: Cotton on top of Turkish rug (4)

indicatorNotes.top of: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee

annotation.surface: Cotton fibres sit on a Turkish carpet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' is British for 'catch on'. 'Cotton' looks like a fabric sitting on a rug.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal synonyms: both mean to grasp something that was not obvious at first.

entries.clue: One’s pens stay in the same place (6)

indicatorNotes.pens: to pen is to enclose, so I'M encloses BIDE

annotation.surface: A person's writing pens are kept in one place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' is a contraction of 'one is', which in the first person is I'M; 'pens' is a verb, not the writing tools.
annotation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for 'in the same place', used in references as ibid.

entries.clue: Lie about end of war and conflict (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of around, so the lie surrounds what follows
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: Propaganda about the end of a war breeds strife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but here it means around: the lie goes round the R.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: friction between people is the rubbing of disagreement, hence conflict.

entries.clue: Passionate desire left American close to derangement (4)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: An American was driven nearly mad by overwhelming longing.
annotation.walkthrough: L for left and US for American are standard crossword abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lust is strong craving, often but not only sexual.
